content: On November 2, 2022, a study was conducted comparing the use of steroids versus standard of care (SOC) or placebo in the treatment of COVID-19. The following outcomes were analyzed using forest plots: 1. All-cause mortality: A comparison was made between patients treated with steroids and those receiving SOC or placebo to evaluate overall mortality rates. 2. All-cause mortality (severe vs. non-severe cases): The analysis differentiated between severe and non-severe cases of COVID-19 to assess mortality outcomes in these subgroups. 3. All-cause mortality by type: Mortality outcomes were further categorized based on specific types or classifications of patients. 4. Time to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV): The time required for patients to need invasive mechanical ventilation was compared between the steroid and SOC/placebo groups. 5. Clinical recovery: The rate and extent of clinical recovery were assessed in patients receiving steroids versus SOC or placebo. 6. Serious adverse events: The incidence of serious adverse events was compared between the two groups to evaluate safety profiles. 7. ICU admission: The need for intensive care unit (ICU) admission was analyzed in both groups. 8. Time to clinical improvement: The duration required for clinical improvement was compared between patients treated with steroids and those receiving SOC or placebo. 9. Length of hospital stay: The total duration of hospitalization was evaluated for both groups. 10. Ventilator-free days: The number of days patients remained free from mechanical ventilation was compared between the two groups. 11. Number of discharged patients: The total number of patients discharged from the hospital was analyzed for both treatment groups. 12. Need for IMV or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO): The requirement for advanced respiratory support, such as IMV or ECMO, was compared between the steroid and SOC/placebo groups. These analyses were conducted using Review Manager (RevMan) software version 5.4.1, and the results were presented in a series of forest plots to visually represent the comparative outcomes.
